articles.title: GOTY 2026’s Final Nomination Is a Battleground of 8/10 Games
articles.summary: One rung below this level, though — alright, maybe two rungs below, after the likes of Resident Evil Requiem and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave — exists a mass of big games that were solid, impressive, and roundly satisfying, all of which got good-but-maybe-not-great reviews from critics.
body: Has 2026 been a vintage year for games? Arguably not. There's been plenty of good stuff to play, there always is. But, at this late stage in the year, we've yet to see any games that rise above and make a bid for modern classic status. There's been no Clair Obscur, no Baldur's Gate 3. And average review scores, across the board, are down. At present, only three new games — not remakes or reissues or expansions — have attained the magic 90-plus rating on review aggregation site Metacritic.
007 First Light. Gears of War: E-Day. Star Wars: Zero Company. Pragmata. Saros. Onimusha: Way of the Sword. Nioh 3. Control Resonant. The Blood of Dawnwalker.

articles.title: Nivalis Nights dares to ask what if Cyberpunk 2077 met Dave the Diver and Stardew Valley? And for now at least I'm loving the answer
articles.summary: As I throw open the windows on my first day in Nivalis, breathing in the city's neon-streaked air and watching the smog roil across the blackened sky, my government-mandated AI automata informs me the district is in lockdown and a serial killer's on the loose.
body: It is, though, kind of fascinating as it starts from a familiar point and begins building outward. It's also, for context, the follow-up to developer Ion Lands' enjoyable neo-noir delivery adventure Cloudpunk, taking that game's stylish dystopia and reimagining it as the setting for a sort of mash-up of Cyberpunk 2077, Stardew Valley, and Dave the Diver. It's an odd mix, certainly, but it works.

A lot of its early success is down to Nivalis itself. Cloudpunk's city was mostly designed to be viewed from afar, but Nivalis Nights plays out in first-person, demanding a world that can withstand closer scrutiny. And Ion Lands more than rises to the challenge. This Nivalis might still be a world built from jagged pixel-art edges, but it's a richly detailed, wonderfully evocative one (stubbornly wonky framerate aside); a chance to live your own little Blade Runner life, right down to the Vangelis-inspired soundtrack.

articles.title: 65 Years Ago, The Twilight Zone Aired Its Creepiest Episode
articles.summary: The Twilight Zone ’s terror successfully bypassed television censorship of the 1960s with speculative fiction. Over five seasons, Serling, as host and writer, examined science, superstition, prejudice, and identity.
body: Horror that doesn’t reside in literal liminal spaces manifests in surreal realities. This transitional space, known as the “twilight zone,” doesn’t adhere to the rules of human society. Rod Serling knew it well. His acclaimed horror anthology series explored stories that were disturbing and unusual, often ending with a twist and a moral lesson.

“His name is Anthony Fremont. He's six years old with a cute little-boy face and blue guileless eyes. But when those eyes look at you, you'd better start thinking happy thoughts. Because the mind behind them is absolutely in charge. This is the Twilight Zone.”

Anthony (Billy Mumy) has used his god-like mental powers to create a tyrannical society with no true sense of freedom. Anthony is not doing anything out of malice. He has never been disciplined by his parents, which is why he is clueless about morality and its consequences.
points: The Twilight Zone ’s terror successfully bypassed television censorship of the 1960s with speculative fiction.
Over five seasons, Serling, as host and writer, examined science, superstition, prejudice, and identity.
Horror that doesn’t reside in literal liminal spaces manifests in surreal realities.
This transitional space, known as the “twilight zone,” doesn’t adhere to the rules of human society.

articles.title: 5 Incredible Anime Arcs That Are 10/10, No Notes
articles.summary: Consider the Chimera Ant arc from Hunter x Hunter, which is nothing short of a rite of passage. It pushes the anime’s deconstruction of shonen conventions to its limits while sending Gon Freecss and Killua Zoldyck down starkly different paths.
body: An exceptional story arc can elevate even a flawed anime series. Although the mechanics of a great arc vary, the best tend to raise the stakes, test their characters, and build steadily toward a cathartic payoff. The conflict must also feel convincing, with the antagonist’s evolving goals and the heroes’ shifting motivations driving the story forward.

Perfection is subjective, but the finest anime arcs share a few qualities: They’re memorable, well-paced, emotionally compelling, and resolved in a meaningful way. With those standards in mind, these five story arcs come remarkably close to perfection. We wouldn’t change a thing.
What happens when a brilliant story ends with an equally brilliant final arc?

Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is filled with memorable stretches, from its exploration of the Ishvalan War to the heroes’ hunt for the Homunculi. But the anime saves its best for last with the Promised Day arc, a chaotic culmination of Father’s 400-year plan for Amestris and the intertwined destinies of Edward and Alphonse Elric.
points: Consider the Chimera Ant arc from Hunter x Hunter, which is nothing short of a rite of passage.

articles.title: The Sunday Papers
articles.summary: Sundays are for having the first lie-in in a month. No trips to visit family, no waking in unfamiliar beds, and, best of all, no having to wait until the hosts are up before you can get started on breakfast.
body: Once that's all polished away, I will return to bed with a fresh cup of coffee and peruse the week's best writing at my own leisure.
What's that? You want me to share? Fine. You can have a read of them when I'm done.

Papers, Please is a game that emerged from the time developer Lucas Pope spent in immigration queues while travelling in Asia and the US. Every interaction with a border officer becomes an exercise in defining yourself, verifying yourself, and proving your existence is recognised. It's an experience many us may be able to relate to, but in an essay for Deleted Saves Micaela Deitz finds a new poignancy to the game.

Filmmakers like Andrei Tarkovsky and Konstantin Lopushansky also took a more philosophical approach to these fantastical settings, focusing on…
body: Soviet sci-fi pushed the boundaries of the genre long before its amplification during the Space Race. One of the most enduring Soviet silent classics is about space travel: Yakov Protazanov’s Aelita (1924), which explores the mundane realities of post-civil war Moscow while championing early sci-fi elements. Aelita, however, was released during an age of radical experimentation, which would soon come to an end due to heavy state censorship until the late 1950s. Although censorship was comparatively lax throughout the ‘60s and ‘70s, any overt political dissent or unorthodox filmmaking was met with pushback.

body: This latest look at the new Marvel Cinematic Universe movie was shared on social media as part of this weekend's San Diego Comic-Con Málaga in Spain. It was an event that saw stars like Anthony Mackie, Winston Duke, and David Harbor make an appearance, with this latest look coming arriving as a little more than a high-res look at Robert Downey Jr.'s take on a classic comic book villain.

Doctor Doom takes center stage in the new Avengers: Doomsday poster. He's looking as menacing as ever, striking a pose similar to the one we've seen before but with somewhat better lighting. The real highlight from the new poster, however, is the three Latverian witches standing behind him.

These three witches – and their hidden identities – have been the subject of much debate amongst MCU fans the last few months. These same mystery characters brought their purple, red, and green robes to San Diego Comic-Con in California this past July. The average onlooker might assume these characters will be little more than henchmen to be discarded in a massive CGI fight sequence, but some aren't so convinced.

articles.title: Inde Navarrette Teases X-Men Role, Says She's 'Doing Everything Humanly Possible' to Do Rogue Justice
articles.summary: Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men, saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice. The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) X-Men reboot movie has a lot to live up to.
body: The actress, who was picked to play the power-siphoning superhero earlier this year, told the LA Times that she's not taking her role in the reboot lightly. In fact, she's doing anything but.

"I'm doing everything humanly possible because I love that character," Navarrette said. "I've studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like. I’m doing everything, exclamation point."

Having parts in shows like 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois means Navarrette has been on TV screens for years, but her role as Nikki in low-budget horror phenomenon Obsession took her fame to a new level. Through all of the Oscar buzz and turned-down parts, it was Schreier's X-Men she decided to sign on to for one of her first post-Obsession roles.

Playing Rogue in X-Men means stepping into the shoes of a character with decades of history. Aside from the Mississippi-born mutant's history in comics, she's also already appeared in numerous animated and live-action projects, with actress Anna Paquin portraying her in films like the 2000 X-Men movie and X2: X-Men United.

body: One of the things the feature focuses on is the satirical side of Grand Theft Auto, mentioning that in GTA 6, alongside radio talk shows and ads, you might overhear a robovoiced phonecall for a political campaign. The world will be full of real-world details, but amplified.

"It needs to wash over you when you're sprinting down the busiest street in the city, hearing snatches of a hundred different conversations as you go," according to James Horton, whose job title is writing director: open world. "If you shift your focus onto something new, it's going to fill the frame, and it's going to push back."

"If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today's world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face," Rupert Humphries, senior vice president of narrative said. "Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world."

articles.title: Everything We Saw at RuneFest 2026, Including RuneScape 4 and RuneScape Reignited
articles.summary: RuneFest 2026 is over, and we’ve got a roundup of everything announced at Jagex’s big show celebrating its long-running fantasy MMORPG. RuneScape 4. This year saw a number of significant announcements, none bigger than confirmation that a fourth RuneScape MMO is in the works.
body: Jagex announced a new RuneScape animated adaptation, in partnership with YouTuber Charlie White, aka MoistCr1TiKaL, and production company Lyrical Media. No word on what this is exactly or when it will be released, but it’s happening!

We also got what Jagex called “the biggest roadmap in the game’s history.” 2027 content unfolds in three story arcs, all of which tie into long-running storylines. Hoard of Dragons (January) offers a sequel to the popular Dragon Slayer quest, City of Gnomes continues the gnome storyline, and Secrets of Karamja introduces a new endgame raid. Also coming is an Agility skill rework, new skilling and solo bosses, new area expansions, and a new Grandmaster Quest.

Old School RuneScape, meanwhile, got an updated roadmap. The Golden Gates to Menaphos are opening finally after 20 years, alongside a suite of fan-demanded content. The Fractured Archive, a new endgame raid, launches October 20. Hardcore Worlds launches November 4. And next year will also see the continuation of the Fairytale questline, Quest month, Dungeons of Gielinor, a Mining and Smithing rework, Chosen Commander, and the Tower of Xorphoros.

articles.title: One of the most popular Total War: Warhammer 3 mods was 'deliberately corrupted' by its creator to sabotage AI-made copies
articles.summary: Total War: Warhammer 3's Lords of the End Times expansion is huge, which is great for us but not so great for all the modders who need to update their work to be compatible with it.
body: It must be galling then to see someone vibe-coding your mod to be compatible with the update, then reuploading it as their own—just another of the AI-coded submods of your work plastered across the Steam Workshop, usually with some ugly AI-generated artwork as the cherry on top.

"Due to the growing number of unauthorized reuploads of SFO: Grimhammer III," Venris, the mod's creator, posted on Patreon, "and more importantly, the use of AI in the process, I have deliberately corrupted the mod to prevent it from functioning with such unauthorized uploads. If this situation continues to escalate, I will make SFO: Grimhammer III private.

"SFO: Grimhammer is the result of nearly ten years of passion and love for this community and the fantasy world. As such, I do not permit anyone to take my work without permission. Especially not for AI-related purposes."
Venris concluded with the call to "Support modders, not AI" and a note that "SFO mods were, are and always will be free for everyone as long as I am here. No paywall."

articles.title: Crimson Desert DLC delayed by 2 weeks, please join me in wishing the devs a fond 'take your time, please drink some water'
articles.summary: Crimson Desert dev Pearl Abyss has announced that its Charting the Unknown DLC will now release on October 29, two weeks on the dot after its original planned launch of October 15.
body: News writer Harvey Randall expressed a similar sentiment in August when Pearl Abyss announced it was slowing down the pace of free updates to Crimson Desert in order to focus on DLC development. Since launch, Crimson Desert has added new critters, new chests, a shotgun, new difficulty options, new mounts, boss rematches⁠—too much, really. I haven't played, but my friend keeps telling me about a "kung-fu button" that's supposedly in the game. Is he pulling my leg? Why would I not believe him at this point?

Charting the Unknown's first trailer contained a lot, but features producer Mollie Taylor fixated on the building construction options, something that reminds me of Skyrim's Hearthfire DLC. Mollie said it also showcased "running on water" and "grabbing onto a shark like some sort of aquatic Uber." What do you do in this game, again?

While the delay indicates this DLC is coming in hot, it hardly even feels like anything amid an industry dominated by increasingly lengthy development times. It's like Pearl Abyss is still blowing out the rest of the field in a 1600m race, but is now out of contention to break a world record. It's fine, man. You did enough.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director says he "did his best" to fight for a full disc release
articles.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi has responded to fans asking for a full disc version of the game, saying he "did [his] best" to push for physical media as the industry edges towards an all-digital future.
body: Speaking to Radio Times, as spotted by IGN, Hamaguchi explained his own attachment to physical media, from buying games as a child to wanting friends and colleagues in the industry to sign copies of their work.

"Personally, obviously, I bought lots of physical editions of games as a child. Sometimes I buy digital editions of games, but if I'm particularly attached to a title, I want to get the physical version," he said, adding that the topic has become "particularly sensitive" in recent months.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will ship with a disc option when it launches in 2027, but PS5 and Xbox Series X players popping in a physical copy will still need to download a hefty chunk of the game to play it in full.
Hamaguchi acknowledged the disc included is a "key disc" containing only the game's opening, and that he understands why some fans have said "no disc, no purchase".

articles.title: Valorant player claims to have inherited hardware ban through secondhand CPU, Riot anticheat boss disputes parts of story
articles.summary: User After-Cartoonist-196 on the German-language PCBaumeister subreddit claims to have bought a CPU secondhand, but that it carried the previous owner's Valorant ban. Extreme surveillance measures have been adopted by esports devs in recent years to combat and punish endemic cheating in their…
body: After-Cartoonist-196's original post was reported on by PC World, and has independently made the rounds on social media as well. They say they bought the CPU on September 21, and that the original owner's ban was logged on August 12.

On Twitter, Koskinas said he was unable to find a support ticket matching After-Cartoonist-196's details, and that the story is "pretty unlikely." Koskinas pointed out that Riot hardware bans have a four month maximum duration, and that Riot support is required to provide the remaining duration of the ban when responding to a ticket.

That does leave much of the original story intact still: If the ban began on August 12, it will not hit the duration limit until mid-December. Koskinas firmly debunked one aspect of the story, though: He denied, in two separate posts, that a system's other hardware is blacklisted when detected alongside a banned component.

videos.title: GT World Series 2026 | Round 3 - Singapore | Nations Cup [ENGLISH]
videos.summary: The 2026 World Series has now passed its halfway mark, with Round 3 taking place in Singapore.
body: In the previous Round in Tokyo, reigning champion José Serrano dominated the race right up until the final lap, only to drop to 5th place due to a costly penalty. This dramatic turn of events has significantly impacted the Points Ranking, in a race where the all the Spaniards were expected to hold the advantage.

Will current leader Kylian Drumont, fresh off his victory in the chaotic Round 2, build momentum to pull away from the pack? Will the Spanish drivers stage a comeback? Or will Valerio Gallo, who has been biding his time and closing in on the leaders, finally launch a serious charge?
With the World Finals fast approaching, the battle for the Nations Cup is becoming increasingly unpredictable. Witness how the competition unfolds!
